1

Details

The question for the meeting. The n_TOF run cannot see X17 (thermal neutrons only, after the γ-flash dead time; backup B5). Can this detector system search for X17 somewhere else, and what does it need?

Short answer. The Micromegas TPCs track well (best chamber 93 % efficient, 1.2° angles, 176 µm intrinsic) and, in the beam, single tracks agree with Geant4 and image the target. The scintillators hold a muon energy scale that predicts electron spectra to 2–5 %. At LNL (⁷Li(p,e⁺e⁻)⁸Be, the ATOMKI reaction) the Geant4 reach is 17 days to 3σ at the ATOMKI ratio as built and about a day with four large plastics. The neutron facilities are much harder (slide 11).

What is still open. At n_TOF the same-chamber Al e⁺e⁻ pairs come in at ⅛ of the Geant4 prediction while the singles agree; until that is understood, the two-track efficiency for soft, close pairs is not demonstrated (slide 7). X17 pairs are a far easier topology.

Hover the dotted terms and the data points for values, counts and provenance. Backup slides follow the main deck.

2

Details

Left: angles. σ68 of (reconstructed − M3 reference) track angle in bins of |reference angle|, det3 (sat_det3, r06 bundle, waveform forward model). Flat from head-on, where a drift-time ladder has no lever arm, to 18°. The cosmic σ68 includes the M3 reference's own error and multiple scattering. Source mpgd26/data/angle_resolution.json.

Middle: efficiency. P(reconstructed within 5 mm of the M3 track) per 15 mm cell, g_det3_wknd, 21,953 reference muons, overall 93.1 %. Detection alone (any hit) is ~100 %; the 5 mm requirement is what the tracking needs. Losses are sparks (~8 %) and far reconstructions.

Right: intrinsic resolution. det4 residuals to the uRWELL track in zones of different telescope pitch, so of different pointing error. σ_res² = pointing² + σ_det4², fitted σ_det4 = 176 ± 10 µm = 0.30 × the 0.78 mm pitch. On the bench the position residual is ~0.45 mm core, dominated by M3 and scattering.

The setups (timeline and drawings: backup). Saclay cosmic bench, June 2026: four M3 reference Micromegas (50×50 cm) track the muons through two MX17 test slots. SPS H4, 31 Jul – 3 Aug 2026: det4 parasitic in the P2 uRWELL test beam, straight high-momentum tracks.

Hits vs waveforms. All geometry here comes from the waveform forward model (Paper II). Per-strip hit times compress the drift ladder by 20–30 % on resistive strips; hit-based angles were 2.4–2.6° on the same data.

3

Details

Maps: per-ray tables of mx_june_wft/report/make_bench_effmaps.py (same datasets as the colleague PDF), binned here in 20 mm cells (cells with < 8 muons left blank). Each map is in the chamber's own frame (make_bench_effmaps.to_detector_frame: the chambers sat at θ ≈ 90° on the bench, so detector y is bench x), which puts dead strips and connector patterns vertical; the outline is the active area. The smooth sliding-kernel version of the same maps is in the backup. Table: mx_june_wft/FLEET_DIGEST.md (r06, five golden keys; det3 there is sat_det3, 93.3 %, the map uses g_det3_wknd, 93.1 %).

What does not work, and why. det6 (C): 14 dead X channels in a connector pattern, 22 % sparking events. det7 (D): sparks in 37 % of events; at n_TOF ~130 of its 512 X channels were dead. det4 (E): 62 % of the area does not amplify, in stripes (det4_sps_assessment), and its amplitude-dependent X width is its dead and weak strips (cloud_basics §35). det2 (B) tracks well but its drift field needs fixing before it can be used for more than tagging. The budget page carries the per-chamber plan: A good, B drift fix, C and D re-bulk, new aluminised-mylar drift windows for all four.

Angles are 1.2° on the two good chambers and ~2–2.5° on the others (fewer, noisier strips per track).

4

Details

Why the Al pairs. After the 1 ms flash veto every neutron is thermal; the trigger fires on the 7.72 MeV Al-capture γ of the capsule vessel (its Compton electrons). About one trigger leg in ten is an e⁺e⁻ made in the capsule. Those pairs are the proof-of-concept sample: ~2 MeV legs that scatter ~9° on the way out (p·β·θ = 0.40 MeV·rad), mostly stop in the wall or the plastic, and land ~25° apart in one chamber. That is the hardest two-track case; X17 legs (8–10 MeV typical) scatter 2.3–2.9°, cross the whole stack and go to opposite chambers.

The expected counts are for the analysed sample: chambers A and C, tracks ≥ 12 ms after the flash, run_69 onward, is2_v2 re-pass. Singles: Geant4 track-like singles per trigger × the efficiency of the digitised reconstruction, times the data triggers. Pairs: the Geant4 ratio of two reconstructable leptons to one × the measured P(2 tracks | 2 leptons), so the opening angle and the close-pair loss are in it. About 10⁸ Al e⁺e⁻ are made per 30 days (Athens: external conversion 7.8×10⁷ + internal pairs 1.4×10⁷); these are the ones the chambers can record.

What we can do with the data, for proof of concept: (1) single tracks against Geant4 (rate, source image, angle scale on cosmic muons); (2) the scintillator response and energy scale track by track; (3) the correlated same-chamber pairs (rate, opening angle) against Geant4 pushed through the same reconstruction.

Sources: x17-status-2026-10-15 (sept26_prelim_analysis/make_status_oct15_deck.py, same_chamber_compare.py → cmp_expectation.csv, cmp.meta.json), Athens thermal_accounting.

5

Details

Maps (ntof_scint_stack, ana/eff_map.parquet, the *_full layers on all_late, net of accidentals): P(the layer fired | an MM track points at that cell), 25 mm cells, every trigger > 10 ms after the flash. The arm's own trigger required wall ∧ plastic, so these levels are biased high (the plastic most of all); they show where each counter works, not its unbiased efficiency. Panels drawn with ntof_scint_stack/make_deck.heat_panel (channel edges, bars and PMTs as in the scint-stack note).

Unbiased efficiencies (events another arm triggered, a few thousand tags per arm; B is rough):

armSiPM wallplastic | wall
A91%60%
B70%50%
C80%57%
D75%57%

Plastic | wall is a response probability, not a hole: two in five particles that cross the 3 mm wall stop before the plastic. Self-triggered, the plastic is ≥ 98 % efficient.

Liquids: a muon gives 20–28 mV against a 16–18 mV readout threshold, so they are threshold-limited; A and D (PMT at the side) answer 12–23× more on their PMT half, B and C (PMT on top) only 1.7–4.5×. They also suffered pile-up (67–76 % of pulses had another pulse in their own tail). For the future (trigger_scint/TRIGGER_OPTIONS.md): repairing the liquids is not worth it for acceptance (LS alone 1.2 % pair acceptance, LS OR plastic 4.3 %, vs ~14 % for big plastics).

Single tracks match Geant4 and image the capsule nose

n_TOF A and C, run_69 onward · grey: Geant4 through the same reconstruction · right: late tracks at the beam-axis plane

band crossing

capsule (Al, CFRP)

6

Details

Rate (left, top): data tracks per trigger over the whole run (A 2,146,620, C 1,614,339 tracks in 23,370,294 triggers) against Geant4 track-like singles in acceptance per trigger × the efficiency of the digitised reconstruction (Geant4 events overlaid on real quiet triggers and run through the production reconstruction: 0.537 A, 0.451 C). Data/Geant4 = ×1.25 (A), ×1.15 (C).

Pointing (left, bottom): tracks whose line passes within 15 mm of the measured source, minus a shuffled-angle null, ≥ 20 ms (capsule_tof.py). The data are at least as capsule-pure as Geant4.

Source image (capsule_pose): each late track's line, the density of where lines cross the beam axis plane minus a shuffled null, 4 mm × 20 mm cells, normalised per panel; red dot = the band crossing (pointing estimator, robust to each chamber's efficiency shape). A and C agree: x ≈ −10 mm, height −31 (A) / −35 (C) mm, where Geant4's capsule puts the Al captures (−28 by the same estimator). The capsule outline is drawn at the frame centre (x = 0): the ~10 mm x offset (beam off the frame, or capsule off the beam) is a stated limitation, since no survey exists. The two chambers' u axes point opposite ways, so only a common shift of the pair against the beam could fake the image. The same spot appears at 4–12, 12–20 and 20–75 ms and before and after the 27 July access. The late tracks are delayed (hall die-away, 23.5 ms) neutrons captured on the capsule Al.

Angle scale on cosmic muons (ntof_cosmics): 41 beam-off runs at the production operating point (57.6 h, 5.2 M triggers) put on the n_TOF clock to ~10 ns (clock_match.py). The straight line joining chambers A and C (470 mm apart) is the angle truth for each chamber: the in-situ calibration (drift velocity, kernel) reproduces it to 1–4 %, in beam-off and in-beam muons alike.

Why this is the best in-situ demonstration: the image needs correct angles and positions in two independent chambers at once, and it reproduces Geant4's source position and rate.

7

Details

Left. Every data track's line extended to the plane through the beam axis (capsule_pose.load_data: height = y at that plane, y up), all is2_v2 cf tracks, normalised to the measured tracks per trigger. Geant4: the nose-first neutron campaign digitised into real quiet triggers and reconstructed (capsule_pose.library, g4_digi), shape normalised to Geant4's own singles per trigger × the digitised efficiency. The data carry an extra tails and a wider core than Geant4 (68 % half-width ~33 vs ~25 mm on the late sample: beam-time background before 12 ms, and real-detector resolution); the peak sits where the capsule-image band crossing puts the source.

Right. Share of tracked events with a second same-chamber track, per ToF bin ≥ 12 ms (points, accidentals included; dotted: the rate-independent part a from f(t) = a + b·rate(t), the correlated pairs). Dashed: the Geant4 prediction, the ratio of two reconstructable leptons to one × the measured P(2 tracks | 2 leptons) of the digitised reconstruction (P(2|2) 0.16 / 0.14), so the opening angle and the close-pair loss are already in it. Correlated pairs: ~2,051 (A), ~1,660 (C). Other efficiency routes bracket data/Geant4 at 0.12–0.52.

Why pairs are not drawn against their pointing origin. The late pair table keeps each leg's position but not its direction, and the pair vertex of two near-parallel ~2 MeV legs (each bent ~9°) lands ~75 mm from where they were born: even perfect tracks pass a 20 mm vertex test 2 % of the time (chance 3 %). A per-leg pointing comparison needs the legs re-joined to their stage-3 lines.

Where the deficit could be. In the detector (two-track loss in busy events): it would hit X17 far less, since X17 legs land in different chambers 470 mm apart, penetrate, fire their own trigger (45 % vs 7.7 %) and vertex to ~10 mm. In the simulation: the capsule model (nose Al, wrap), the delayed-neutron source population, or the reconstruction version the prediction used (one-sided search). Next with the data we have: re-digitise Geant4 pairs with is2_v2; Geant4 with delayed thermal neutrons; check the capsule model; look for a two-lepton trigger effect.

Opening angle (A): the correlated excess prefers the Geant4 e⁺e⁻ shape (χ² 6.6/6 vs 26/6 for unrelated pairs). Source: x17-status-2026-10-15; same_chamber_compare.py, cmp_*.csv.

Every layer sits on Geant4's energy scale

self-triggered single tracks at n_TOF (run_145 for the MM) · points: data · line: Geant4 with the measured trigger and resolution, not refitted

8

Details

Scintillators (ntof_calorimetry/wall_plastic.py, note scint-calorimetry): the SiPM wall and each plastic bar are calibrated on cosmic muons only (beam-off runs on the n_TOF clock, path from the MM track), then Geant4 of the full stack predicts the beam-electron spectra (total prompt deposit in the matched bar, smeared with the measured σ/MPV, the arm's trigger applied in MeV). Drawn at scale 1; the numbers on the plots are the data/Geant4 scales over the whole spectrum. Per bar (≥ 40 ms): plastic A1/A2/C2 1.05/1.03/1.02, C1 1.15 (a pure gain offset of unknown cause); wall A/C 0.95/0.96. Linear from the muon's 3.4 MeV to stopping electrons at 3–8 MeV; stable to 0.5–0.8 % run to run. A 25 mm bar (the run-config text) would put every scale at ×1.27, so the 20 mm in Geant4 is right. Plastic PMTs lose 3–8 % gain 12–25 ms after the flash.

Micromegas dE/dx (mm_edep_*, the track passport): the charge along each track, corrected for the readout window and for an in-situ gain map, in keV per 30 mm at normal incidence. The data median (5.6 keV) matches Heed's MIP; per-track resolution 16 % (A) / 22 % (C) in beam. The simulation is Heed ionisation through the full digitisation and reconstruction.

What the MM adds (Geant4-trained estimators, cross-validated): nothing for fast tracks (the gas is minimum-ionising), but for electrons below 3 MeV the energy width goes 1.56 → 1.35 MeV with the MM; for tracks that never reach the plastic it halves the vertex-energy width of 1–3.5 MeV capsule electrons (1.7 → 0.45–0.8 MeV). It also tags tracks with several particles in the gap (AUC 0.84; the wall cannot: 0.46–0.48), which is what a two-track candidate needs. The track angle buys back the energy of steep tracks (1.4 → 1.1 MeV). Event displays of a single-lepton and a several-particle track are in the backup.

For the future. At n_TOF the 2 cm plastic stops only the soft leg (a range telescope). With 4–5 cm plates the full stack is a calorimeter: the LNL E_sum and pair-mass fits rest on this n_TOF-anchored response (as built it loses the mass fit, backup). Resolution of a thick plate: to be measured on a prototype.

LNL: enough X17 in days; the IPC shape is the work

⁷Li(p,e⁺e⁻)⁸Be at the 18.15 MeV resonance, 1 µA · Geant4 of the n_TOF apparatus, MM 15° + TOF, θ × |y| × E_sum fit

9

Details

Reach (x17_facility_search/lnl/, FEASIBILITY_SIM.md §12–18, lnl/out/talk/numbers.json): days to 3σ at R(ATOMKI) = 5.8×10⁻⁶ with the θ × |y| × E_sum fit. Pair trigger (Geant4): as built 3.3%, big plastics 23.2%. ~900 X17 made per day at 1 µA.

Left, bottom. X17 at the ATOMKI ratio after 30 days at 1 µA, inside the fit, against the ≈ 2 X17 made in the whole n_TOF thermal window (before any acceptance). Why it works where n_TOF could not: DC beam, no γ flash, so the DAQ is 91–98 % live up to 4 µA, at the exact ATOMKI kinematics.

Middle. The opening-angle distribution for one week with big plastics: grey = background (IPC M1 and E1, γ₁ pairs, cosmics after the MM-tracked veto), red = with X17 at R(ATOMKI) (m = 16.7 MeV) (lnl/out/nd/maps/proj.csv). In 1D the X17 is a few % of the counts at 125–155°: a background-shape error of a few % competes with the signal, so the IPC (and any other contamination) has to be known and subtracted very well. In-run controls: the E_p scan moves the X17 edge (~10° over the scanned energies), off-resonance points, symmetric pairs.

Right. S/B per cell of opening angle × energy split |y| (E_sum 14–19 MeV, 3° × 0.05 cells, cells with < 3 background pairs per week blank; dashed: where a 16.7 MeV X17 lands). The X17 follows the constant-mass curve; the IPC (a virtual photon of any mass) fills the plane. Impostor test: a background error that copies the X17 angle spectrum exactly reads as 100 % of an X17 in an angle-only fit and 13–24 % in the θ × |y| × E_sum fit, with χ² ≈ 20 left over. So the energy measurement makes the search resilient to background-modelling errors (LNL note, slides "2D counts" and "impostor").

Pseudo-data check (§17): one simulated week at R(ATOMKI), blinded, truth differing from the fit model: r̂ = 0.87 ± 0.14 (6.1σ); errors honest up to a week, a wider fit needed at 30 days. Risks: scattering in the target chamber (1.0 d at 4.5° → 6.8 d at the n_TOF capsule's ~14°), cosmics, IPC shape. LNL's own ⁸Be spectrometer ran there in 2023–24. The drawing follows the LNL note's set-up slide (transverse, pinwheel offset not drawn); a 3D view is lnl/viz/lnl_setup_3d.html.

10

Details

The curve (lnl/plastic_size.py, an analytic stand-in for a Geant4 size scan): straight leptons from a 2 mm beam spot through the surveyed MM active area, Highland kicks in the MM and the SiPM wall, a leg must cross a read-out SiPM bar and the plastic face above an energy threshold. Two free numbers are fitted to the Geant4 pair tag as built and with 75×75 cm plastics. Days to 3σ scale as B/S² in 125–155°, anchored to the Geant4 big-plastics value; E_sum, MM 15° and TOF efficiencies are held at their Geant4 values, so it is about geometry only. Where the plates would collide with their neighbours they are pushed back (beyond ~75 cm).

Why it flattens: past ~65–75 cm the plate covers the whole cone of leptons that crossed an MM (92 % of X17 leptons at 75×75); the SiPM wall (83 %) is then the cap. Removing the wall (orange) leaves a plastic-only leg and gains a little more, but the wall stays: it is the trigger and a tracking point, so only the curve with the plates where the bars are now is drawn.

Prototype plate (trigger_scint, optics toy): 78 × 80 × 5 cm polystyrene, fishtail guides, a 3" PMT at each end; read all 20 SiPM bars (×1.4 on acceptance); FERS-5200 for the 160 SiPM ends (~€18k). Toy: ~77 pe/MeV, 4 % non-uniformity with two ends, σt ≈ 124 ps at 5 MeV; ~15 %/√E, about 5 % at a 10 MeV deposit. All-in with the SiPM readout ~€121k. Whole LNL run budget: Lean €98k · Self-sufficient €174k · Upgrade €286k. Before buying: one plate on the cosmic bench (light yield, uniformity against an MM map, linearity to 12 MeV).

Costs (budgetary, EUR 2026, no labour/VAT): scintillator PVT 0.6 €/cm³, PS 0.25 €/cm³; PMT + divider 3" €3.3k; guides €0.8–1.5k; wrapping €1.5–5k per slab; HV + digitizer €1.4k per PMT. Get quotes (Eljen/Luxium PVT, Nuvia/Epic PS). Run budget: dylan-neff.web.cern.ch/facilities/budget.html (collaborator comments enabled).

Details

n_TOF: mpgd26 / ntof_athens_26 (the Athens deck): the γ flash saturates DREAM (detector recovers in 2 µs, DREAM in 5 ms); every volt of gain costs ms of beam; the run moved to thermals, where (n,p) dominates and the ³He self-shields: 4.4 → 0.07 X17/day in 0.01–0.1 eV, ≈100 → ≈2 X17 made over the campaign's 436,373 pulses. Below ~2 eV only s-wave channels are open (M1, and E0 with no real photon; CLAUDE.md / ipc_born.py).

ILL (ill/FEASIBILITY_SIM.md §13): He flight tube + Be 0.25 mm (or 25 µm mylar) window cut the trigger rate 249 → 8–23 Hz and halve the MM occupancy; with a ceiling cosmic panel and E_sum > 14 MeV the reach is 6.5×10⁻³ at 1.9×10¹⁰ n/s and 5.3×10⁻³ at 6×10¹⁰ with a Ø4 cm spot (×3.2 from ⁸Be). Walls: MM occupancy + DREAM (3.4×10⁻³ if both cut ×10), then IPC statistics (2.1×10⁻³ at 1.2×10¹¹, ×1.3). Spin selection with polarised n + ³He is the extra lever (POLARISED.md). ³He: bare mylar loses ~22 L per cycle → the PET + Al laminate skin (he4_bag §6).

Sketch: G1 (HANDOFF_SIM §4): 1 bar, 300 mm of gas, R 40 mm, entrance window at y_w = −21.6 mm so the median capture sits at the MM centre; 99.5 % of the H113 beam stops inside; downstream cap at +278 mm (1.2 % of vertices beyond the +180 mm MM edge). The ⁴He "pre-chamber" is the flight tube from the aperture to the cell window: ⁴He captures no neutrons and scatters ~13× less than air; ~90 % of the air ¹⁴N(n,γ) is on that 300 mm path. A balloon around the whole cell is not worth it (⁴He permeates into the cell and the MM gas). Shading = capture density along the cell (schematic exponential with the G1 median).

Demokritos (NCSR Demokritos, Athens): a Tandem that makes quasi-monoenergetic MeV neutrons. Not studied in x17_facility_search yet: no flux fold and no reach, hence the "?"; the expectation is that the rate is too low.

NFS (ganil_nfs/README.md §7, §9): d+Be peaks at 17 MeV, measured only above 1.5 MeV; options: lower deuteron energy, D(d,n)³He monoenergetic (~2.45 MeV, may never have been built), ⁷Li(p,n) near threshold. The X17 shoulder slides to 99° at 2 MeV and 66° at 14 MeV, into the IPC-rich region.

12

Details

Order: I and II together (I cites II for every position, angle and drift velocity). III needs the pair rate question settled or stated as a limitation; IV carries the facility reach so III stays about the data.

Papers I and II (decision 2026-10-08, PAPER_PLAN.md): the cosmic bench and SPS in both; post to arXiv on the same day as companions. Biggest open items: hits vs waveforms on the same events (R1–R5), timing on waveforms (D3), reproducing the r06 numbers for quoting (done for the golden keys, C1), the calibration freeze (on hold).

Paper III: written as a demonstrator: the station, the run and its limits (flash, thermal-only, noise step on 23 July), the single tracks and capsule image against Geant4, the scintillator stack and energy scale, the Al pair analysis with the ⅛ rate stated as an open result, and the lessons that feed LNL.

Paper IV (optional): the full Geant4 of the apparatus, the thermal accounting, the IPC expectation (M1 + E0, ipc_born.py) and the facility reach (LNL 3D fit, ILL, NFS). Splitting it keeps III about the data.

13

Details

Each pixel is the fraction of reference muons reconstructed within 5 mm under a Gaussian-weighted circle (σ = 4 mm) swept across the face in 0.5 mm steps: mpgd26/make_efficiency_map.gaussian_sliding through mx_june_wft/report/make_bench_effmaps.make_map, the kernel of the MPGD26 efficiency slide. Pixel-to-pixel texture is counting noise (≈ 7 effective muons per kernel; independent-circle variance is 1.07× binomial away from the edges). The 20 mm cells of the fleet slide trade resolution for less noise.

14

Details

The track passport (ntof_calorimetry/track_passport.py, note track-passport). Left: a single lepton that goes through the plastic (the liquid fires). Right: a track with a high gas deposit that the Geant4-trained estimator tags as several particles in the gap, the signature a two-track candidate leaves when the tracks overlap. Energies and P(several) come from Geant4-trained estimators (model-dependent); the counters carry their measured resolutions (wall ~16–18 %, plastic ~4–7 % at the MIP), the gas deposit its per-track resolution.

Details

Timeline sources. mpgd26/make_timeline.py (the MPGD26 project timeline): EAR2 tests from the run tables on EOS; bench span from mx_june_cosmic_qa; n_TOF from ntof_run_report (162 runs, 2,705 sub-runs, 17.9 TB, 41.8 M events); SPS from sps_beam_test_26/analysis/RUN_TIMELINE.md.

Chamber names. The same chamber has a bench name and an n_TOF arm: det3 = A, det2 = B, det6 = C, det7 = D; det4 = "E", the SPS chamber.

Bench geometry (scenes_bench.py): scintillators at z −110 and 1420 mm, M3 at 24, 144, 1185, 1302 mm, test slots P1 232 and P2 702 mm. SPS (scenes_sps.py): uRWELL at 0 and 1370 mm, P2 fans at 320/630/940 mm, det4 in the ~25 cm between the last P2 and the back uRWELL.

At thermal energies only s-wave channels are open (M1, and E0 with no real photon), (n,p) takes 92 % of the neutrons and the ³He self-shields. The ²⁷Al pairs (~10⁸ per 30 days) became the demonstrator.

The capsule wall is 83 % of the n_TOF budget; after the upgrade 63 % is air. The 109° shoulder returns: peak height ×0.22 → ×0.50, FWHM 37° → 11°.

m_ee alone degrades much faster (1.7 → 284 d); the 3D fit is robust.

Thermal capture at rest covers the s-wave half of the physics only; the reference ratio 2.5×10⁻² would be a ~6–9σ effect in one cycle with timing + veto (ill/README.md).
